proof: Write h=sqrt(3)/2, the altitude of an actual side1 grid triangle. The exact gray vertices are (2,0),(9/2,0),(9/2,5h),(2,4h). Parallel vertical sides have lengths4h and5h, separated by5/2. Trapezoid area=(5/2)(4h+5h)/2=45h/4. One smallest equilateral triangle has area h/2, hence gray area=45/2=22.5 units. The gray top is not horizontal; all fractional cells are included. No piece-count approximation is used.
new_error: A side2 equilateral grid triangle has area4 of these units. Treating the matched complete side2 triangle as area1 gives (45/2)/4=45/8=5.625, a specific wrong numeric answer.
